subject: scoping issue:  Shiny object found before object of same name in Global Env

messages.author: 33dc9c6d026ee296
messages.subject: scoping issue:  Shiny object found before object of same name in Global Env
parts:
I have an Addin that creates and runs code based on user input.  The code is created as a string and then evaluated with eval-parse.

The relevant code is as follows:

command <- rv$code  # rv is a list of reactive values, rv$code is the code to run
eval(parse(text = command))

Suppose that a data framed named "a" is in the user's Global Environment when the Addin is called, and  user input results in rv$code having the value "xtabs(~ group, data = a)".  Then we would expect a table of the values of the variable "group" in the data frame "a".  Instead we get an error:  "'data' argument is of the wrong type."

I did some checking.  If you modify the relevant code as follows:

command <- rv$code
print(command)
print(a)
print(search())
eval(parse(text = command))

You discover that:

* The command-text is as expected.
* What's printed as "a" is the Shiny function tag$a, not the data frame a.
* Nevertheless, the Global Environment appears first on the search path, before the Shiny namespace.

Why, in the call to eval(), does R find the anchor-tag function instead of the data frame?

Thanks for any insight you can provide.
